market.title: EU Instant Payments Mandate: Corporates Face Implementation Hurdles
market.summary_short: European corporates are grappling with the impending mandatory rollout of instant payments, facing significant technical and operational challenges. Banks are also under pressure to ensure readiness for the new regulatory deadlines.
market.summary_detail: The EU's Instant Payments Regulation, aiming for ubiquitous real-time transactions, is creating substantial pressure on corporate treasuries and banks alike. While the regulation mandates banks to offer instant payments at no extra cost by early 2027 for incoming and mid-2027 for outgoing payments, corporates must adapt their internal systems and processes. Many companies, especially SMEs, are still evaluating the full impact on their liquidity management, reconciliation, and fraud prevention strategies. The shift requires significant IT investments and changes to existing payment workflows, with concerns about the readiness of all participants across the CEE region.
key_points: Mandatory instant payments for incoming transactions by early 2027.
Outgoing instant payments mandated by mid-2027.
No additional charges for instant payments compared to standard credit transfers.
Significant IT and process adjustments required for corporates and banks.
market.rbi_cash_management: This regulation is critical for CMIplus, driving demand for real-time payment capabilities across all channels (EBICS, H2H, API). RBI must ensure its network banks are fully compliant and CMIplus offers robust, seamless instant payment processing, including enhanced reconciliation and fraud prevention features, to support its corporate clients in CEE.

market.title: PSD3 and Open Finance: New Era for European Payment Services
market.summary_short: The European Commission's proposed PSD3 and Open Finance Framework signals a major overhaul for payment services and financial data sharing. This initiative aims to enhance consumer protection, combat fraud, and expand the scope of open banking.
market.summary_detail: The new legislative package, including PSD3 and the Open Finance Framework (OFS), seeks to modernize the existing PSD2. Key objectives include strengthening user rights, improving fraud prevention mechanisms, and fostering greater competition in the financial sector. For corporates, this means potential for more sophisticated API-driven cash management solutions, but also increased compliance burdens related to data access and security. The OFS, in particular, could extend data sharing beyond payments to other financial products, creating new opportunities for integrated treasury services and liquidity management across CEE.
key_points: PSD3 aims to replace and enhance PSD2, focusing on fraud and consumer rights.
Open Finance Framework (OFS) extends data sharing beyond payments.
Increased regulatory scrutiny on third-party providers (TPPs).
Potential for new API-driven treasury and liquidity management solutions.
market.rbi_cash_management: PSD3 and OFS will profoundly impact RBI's Open Banking strategy and CMIplus API offerings. RBI must proactively adapt its API infrastructure to meet new regulatory requirements, enhance security, and leverage expanded data access to deliver innovative, value-added services for corporate clients, especially in the CEE region.

market.title: EBICS 3.0 Adoption Accelerates, ISO 20022 Benefits Emerge
market.summary_short: German and European corporates are increasingly adopting EBICS 3.0, driven by its enhanced security and multi-bank capabilities. The full potential of ISO 20022 data enrichment is also becoming clearer, offering significant treasury benefits.
market.summary_detail: The migration to EBICS 3.0 continues to gain momentum, with more banks and corporates recognizing its advantages, including improved encryption standards and streamlined multi-bank connectivity. While the technical transition presents challenges, the long-term benefits for secure and efficient payment communication are substantial. Concurrently, treasurers are beginning to fully leverage the rich data capabilities of ISO 20022 messages, moving beyond basic payment processing to advanced reconciliation, cash forecasting, and liquidity management. This data richness, combined with EBICS 3.0, promises a new era of automated and insightful treasury operations across Europe, including the CEE region.

Migration to EBICS 3.0 is accelerating among corporates and banks.

market.title: EU Mandates Instant Payments, ISO 20022 Adoption Accelerates
market.summary_short: The European Union has finalized regulations making instant payments mandatory for all banks, significantly accelerating the adoption of ISO 20022 for cross-border transactions. This move aims to enhance liquidity management and payment efficiency across the Eurozone and beyond.
market.summary_detail: The European Parliament and Council have formally approved the new Instant Payments Regulation, requiring all EU banks to offer instant credit transfers in Euro within 10 seconds, at no extra cost compared to standard transfers. This regulation also mandates full ISO 20022 migration for all payment messages, including cross-border, by early 2027, pushing corporates to upgrade their treasury systems. The move is expected to boost real-time liquidity management, reduce payment processing times, and foster greater financial integration within the CEE region. Banks are now scrambling to ensure compliance and upgrade their infrastructure to meet the strict deadlines, with penalties for non-compliance looming.

market.title: Open Banking APIs Drive Corporate eBAM and Liquidity Innovation
market.summary_short: The adoption of Open Banking APIs is rapidly transforming corporate treasury, enabling advanced eBAM functionalities and real-time liquidity management. This shift allows corporates to gain unprecedented visibility and control over their global cash positions.
market.summary_detail: Corporate treasurers are increasingly leveraging Open Banking APIs to automate bank account management (eBAM) processes, from opening and closing accounts to managing mandates and signatories digitally. This technological advancement provides real-time access to account information, balances, and transaction data across multiple banks and regions, significantly improving liquidity forecasting and cash pooling efficiency. The standardization of APIs, driven by initiatives like PSD3, is further accelerating this trend, allowing for seamless integration with ERP and TMS systems. Companies are reporting reduced operational costs and enhanced fraud detection capabilities through these integrated solutions.

market.title: AI-Powered Fraud Prevention Critical Amid Rising Payment Scams
market.summary_short: Financial institutions and corporates are increasingly deploying AI-powered solutions to combat the surge in sophisticated payment fraud, particularly with the rise of instant payments. Proactive measures are essential to protect against evolving cyber threats.
market.summary_detail: The rapid adoption of instant payment schemes, while beneficial for speed, has also created new avenues for fraudsters, leading to a significant increase in payment scams and cyber-attacks. AI and machine learning are becoming indispensable tools for real-time fraud detection, analyzing vast datasets to identify anomalous transaction patterns and suspicious activities. Banks are investing heavily in advanced security protocols, including multi-factor authentication and behavioral biometrics, to safeguard corporate accounts and transactions. Collaboration between banks, corporates, and technology providers is vital to share threat intelligence and develop robust, adaptive fraud prevention strategies in the face of ever-evolving threats.

market.title: EU Instant Payments Mandate Accelerates ISO 20022 Adoption
market.summary_short: The European Union's new Instant Payments Regulation is driving banks to accelerate their ISO 20022 migration efforts. This mandate requires all EU/EEA banks to offer instant credit transfers within specific timelines, leveraging the richer data capabilities of ISO 20022.
market.summary_detail: The recently enacted EU Instant Payments Regulation (IPR) sets ambitious deadlines for payment service providers (PSPs) in the EU and EEA to offer instant credit transfers. By early 2027, all PSPs must be able to receive instant payments, and by early 2028, they must offer instant payment sending capabilities. This regulation is a significant catalyst for the full adoption of ISO 20022 messaging, as the standard's enhanced data fields are crucial for efficient processing, fraud screening, and compliance reporting required by instant payments. The IPR also introduces measures to ensure affordability and accessibility, including a cap on instant payment fees. This move is expected to significantly boost liquidity management and real-time reconciliation for corporates across Europe, including the CEE region.

market.title: Open Banking APIs Transform Corporate Treasury Operations

Corporates are utilizing APIs to connect directly with their banks, pulling real-time account balances, transaction data, and initiating payments directly from their ERP or TMS systems. This direct connectivity eliminates manual processes, reduces reconciliation times, and provides an unprecedented level of cash visibility across multiple bank relationships and currencies. While security and standardization remain key considerations, the benefits in terms of efficiency, liquidity optimization, and fraud prevention are driving rapid adoption, particularly for multinational corporations operating across diverse banking landscapes like CEE.

market.title: EBICS v3.0 Drives European Cross-Border Payment Modernization
market.summary_short: The adoption of EBICS v3.0 is gaining momentum across Europe, particularly for secure and standardized cross-border payments. This latest version offers enhanced security features and improved compatibility with ISO 20022 messaging.
market.summary_detail: EBICS (Electronic Banking Internet Communication Standard) v3.0 is becoming a preferred channel for corporate-to-bank communication, especially for high-volume and cross-border payments within Europe. Its robust security protocols, including strong encryption and digital signatures, provide a secure alternative to other host-to-host solutions. The key advantage of v3.0 lies in its native support for ISO 20022 XML messages, streamlining data exchange and reducing the need for complex format conversions. This standardization is crucial for corporates managing multi-bank relationships across countries like those in CEE, enabling more efficient payment processing, reconciliation, and reporting. As more banks and corporates migrate to v3.0, it promises to further harmonize the European payment landscape.

The project focuses on key aspects such as privacy, functionality, and governance, with ongoing work on a detailed scheme rulebook to define its operational framework. The Digital Euro is envisioned as a public good, complementing cash, and is designed to be widely accessible, secure, and efficient for everyday payments across the Euro area. Its implementation will have profound implications for the entire payment ecosystem, potentially reshaping retail payment habits and requiring banks to integrate new infrastructure and services.

market.title: Singapore Banks Execute Blockchain-Enabled Transactions on Swift Ledger
market.summary_short: DBS, OCBC, and UOB in Singapore have successfully completed live domestic SGD transactions using tokenised deposits on Swift’s blockchain-based ledger. This marks a significant advancement in the use of distributed ledger technology for interbank payments.
market.summary_detail: Three major Singaporean banks – DBS, OCBC, and UOB – have successfully conducted real-time domestic Singapore dollar transactions utilizing tokenised deposits on Swift's innovative blockchain-based ledger. This pilot demonstrates the viability of integrating distributed ledger technology (DLT) into existing global financial infrastructure like Swift for interbank settlements. The use of tokenised deposits on a blockchain ledger could revolutionize multi-currency payments, enhance liquidity management, and improve the speed and transparency of cross-border transactions. While currently focused on domestic SGD, this initiative sets a precedent for how global payment networks might evolve to support digital currencies and tokenised assets, potentially impacting ISO 20022 adoption and real-time payment systems worldwide.

regulatory.title: EU Regulations Transform Liquidity Management for Instant Payments, PSD3
regulatory.summary_short: A new EBA report analyzes the profound impact of the Instant Payments Regulation (IPR), proposed Payment Services Regulation (PSR), and PSD3 on banks' liquidity management. These regulations are expected to accelerate instant payment adoption and reshape the financial sector's liquidity landscape.
regulatory.summary_detail: The Euro Banking Association (EBA) Liquidity Management Working Group (LMWG) has released a report detailing the far-reaching implications of three critical EU regulatory initiatives: the Instant Payments Regulation (IPR), the proposed Payment Services Regulation (PSR), and the Payment Services Directive 3 (PSD3). The report explores how these measures will drive the uptake of instant payments, foster a level playing field among market participants, and fundamentally alter the liquidity management framework for financial institutions. It highlights the need for banks to adapt their strategies and systems to manage liquidity effectively in a real-time payment environment, ensuring compliance with evolving regulatory requirements and preparing for the transformation of the payment ecosystem.
key_points: Analysis of Instant Payments Regulation (IPR) impact on liquidity.
Assessment of proposed Payment Services Regulation (PSR) implications.
Examination of Payment Services Directive 3 (PSD3) effects on banking.
Focus on transformation of the liquidity management landscape.
regulatory.rbi_cash_management: RBI/CMIplus must assess the report's findings to understand the strategic implications for its liquidity management services and instant payment offerings. This includes evaluating potential adjustments to internal processes, treasury functions, and platform capabilities to ensure readiness for the evolving regulatory environment and client needs.

regulatory.title: EBA Updates Fraud Taxonomy to Align with Forthcoming PSR/PSD3
regulatory.summary_short: The EBA has released version 7.0 of its Fraud Taxonomy, effective 1 January 2027, to harmonise fraud classification across Europe. This update reflects the latest fraud trends and is designed to support information-sharing arrangements under the forthcoming Payment Services Regulation (PSR).
regulatory.summary_detail: The Euro Banking Association (EBA) has published version 7.0 of its EBA Fraud Taxonomy, which will become effective on 1 January 2027. This annual review, supported by fraud experts, ensures the taxonomy remains relevant to evolving fraud trends. Key updates include replacing 'emotional manipulation' with more specific modi like 'support a friend or family member fraud', 'romance fraud', and 'charity / donation fraud', and adding new tags for suspected money mule activity and 'card chip relay' fraud. The taxonomy provides a standardised pan-European framework for classifying payment fraud scenarios, enhancing data comparability, monitoring, reporting, and information sharing, particularly in anticipation of the Payment Services Regulation (PSR) which is part of the PSD3 package.
key_points: New EBA Fraud Taxonomy version 7.0 released.
Effective date for implementation: 1 January 2027.
Updated fraud modi and new labels/tags introduced.
Supports pan-European fraud-fighting and PSR/PSD3 information sharing.
regulatory.rbi_cash_management: RBI/CMIplus must review its internal fraud monitoring systems, reporting frameworks, and data classification to ensure full alignment with EBA Fraud Taxonomy v7.0 by the effective date. This includes updating any automated fraud detection rules and ensuring compliance with future PSR requirements for fraud data sharing, impacting all payment types including instant payments.
